patch:
diff --git a/lib/helpers.bash b/lib/helpers.bash
index 565173ed77..4cc2d57435 100644
--- a/lib/helpers.bash
+++ b/lib/helpers.bash
@@ -181,18 +181,40 @@ _bash-it_update() {
   status="$(git rev-list master..${BASH_IT_REMOTE}/master 2> /dev/null)"
 
   if [[ -n "${status}" ]]; then
-    git pull --rebase &> /dev/null
-    if [[ $? -eq 0 ]]; then
-      echo "Bash-it successfully updated."
-      echo ""
-      echo "Migrating your installation to the latest version now..."
-      _bash-it-migrate
-      echo ""
-      echo "All done, enjoy!"
-      bash-it reload
-    else
-      echo "Error updating Bash-it, please, check if your Bash-it installation folder (${BASH_IT}) is clean."
-    fi
+
+    for i in $(git rev-list --merges master..${BASH_IT_REMOTE}); do
+      num_of_lines=$(git log -1 --format=%B $i | awk 'NF' | wc -l)
+      if [ $num_of_lines -eq 1 ]; then
+        description="%s"
+      else
+        description="%b"
+      fi
+      git log --format="%h: $description (%an)" -1 $i
+    done
+    echo ""
+    read -e -n 1 -p "Would you like to update to $(git log -1 --format=%h origin/master)? [Y/n] " RESP
+    case $RESP in
+      [yY]|"")
+        git pull --rebase &> /dev/null
+        if [[ $? -eq 0 ]]; then
+          echo "Bash-it successfully updated."
+          echo ""
+          echo "Migrating your installation to the latest version now..."
+          _bash-it-migrate
+          echo ""
+          echo "All done, enjoy!"
+          bash-it reload
+        else
+          echo "Error updating Bash-it, please, check if your Bash-it installation folder (${BASH_IT}) is clean."
+        fi
+        ;;
+      [nN])
+        echo "Not upgrading…"
+        ;;
+      *)
+        echo -e "\033[91mPlease choose y or n.\033[m"
+        ;;
+      esac
   else
     echo "Bash-it is up to date, nothing to do!"
   fi
problem_statement:
Add releases/versioning
It would be great to start tagging versions of the bash-it to make it easier to know if we have the latest version available, rollback to an older version in case of issues, etc...

Thanks for this great project!

problem_statement:
node plugin should postpend path instead of prepend
https://github.com/npm/npm/issues/957#issuecomment-237064313 goes into detail why it is generally a bad idea. In short: a malicious package could override a system executable and do whatever it wants.

problem_statement:
Considder adding git switch aliases
I'd love to see some git switch aliases included with the current batch of git aliases. Has this been considered before? Things I'd like:

- `git switch`
- `git switch -c branch`
- `git switch -t branch`

Thanks for your consideration!

problem_statement:
Git Completions Out of Date (completions @ v2.21 vs latest v2.26)
In discussing / working on #1525 for the `git switch`, I realized that the current git completions don't support the `switch` command.

Looking into a bit, I see the lats update to the git completions was:

[@trmaphi : Update bash completion for git v2.21.0](https://github.com/Bash-it/bash-it/commit/c8b4ffbac1f9722c39ae544cf1603c3a05ae202b)

The `switch` command was added to git in v2.23, so that explains why it doesn't work.

I'm creating this issue to:

* Track the fact that the git completions are a bit out of date.
* Give a place to ping @trmaphi to see if they might be interested in updating them? :) 

---
cc: @trmaphi

+     # Enable stuff

+_bash-it-profile-save() {
+  _about 'saves the current configuration to the "profile" directory'
+  _group 'lib'
+
+  local name=$1
+  while [ -z "$1" ]; do
+    read -r -e -p "Please enter the name of the profile to save: " name
+    case $name in
+      "")
+        echo -e "\033[91mPlease choose a name.\033[m"
+        ;;
+      *)
+        break
+        ;;
+    esac
+  done
+
+  local profile_path="${BASH_IT}/profiles/${name}.bash_it"
+  if [ -f "$profile_path" ]; then
+    echo -e "\033[0;33mProfile \"$name\" already exists.\033[m"
+    while true; do
+      read -r -e -n 1 -p "Would you like to overwrite existing profile? [y/N] " RESP
+      case $RESP in
+        [yY])
+          echo -e "\033[0;32mOverwriting profile \"$name\"...\033[m"
+          rm "$profile_path"
+          break
+          ;;
+        [nN] | "")
+          echo -e "\033[91mAborting profile save...\033[m"
+          return 1
+          ;;
+        *)
+          echo -e "\033[91mPlease choose y or n.\033[m"
+          ;;
+      esac
+    done
+  fi
+
+  local something_exists
+  echo "# This file is auto generated by Bash-it. Do not edit manually!" > "$profile_path"
+  for subdirectory in "plugins" "completion" "aliases"; do
+    local component_exists=""
+    echo "Saving $subdirectory configuration..."
+    for f in "${BASH_IT}/$subdirectory/available/"*.bash; do
+      _bash-it-determine-component-status-from-path "$f"
+      if [ "$enabled" == "x" ]; then
+        if [ -z "$component_exists" ]; then
+            # This is the first component of this type, print the header
+            component_exists="yes"
+            something_exists="yes"
+            echo "" >> "$profile_path"
+            echo "# $subdirectory" >> "$profile_path"
+        fi
+        echo "$subdirectory $enabled_file_clean" >> "$profile_path"
+      fi
+    done
+  done
+  if [ -z "$something_exists" ]; then
+    echo "It seems like no configuration was enabled.."
+    echo "Make sure to double check that this is the wanted behavior."
+  fi
+
+  echo "All done!"
+  echo ""
+  echo "Profile location: $profile_path"
+  echo "Load the profile by invoking \"bash-it profile load $name\""
+}
+
+_bash-it-profile-load-parse-profile() {
+  _about 'Internal function used to parse the profile file'
+  _param '1: path to the profile file'
+  _param '2: dry run- only check integrity of the profile file'
+  _example '$ _bash-it-profile-load-parse-profile "profile.bash_it" "dry"'
+
+  local num=0
+  while read -r -a line; do
+    num=$((num + 1))
+    # Ignore comments and empty lines
+    [[ -z "${line[*]}" || "${line[*]}" =~ ^#.* ]] && continue
+    local enable_func="_enable-${line[0]}"
+    local subdirectory=${line[0]}
+    local component=${line[1]}
+
+    typeset to_enable=$(command ls "${BASH_IT}/$subdirectory/available/$component".*bash 2>/dev/null | head -1)
+    # Ignore botched lines
+    if [[ -z "$to_enable" ]]; then
+      echo -e "\033[91mBad line(#$num) in profile, aborting load...\033[m"
+      local bad="bad line"
+      break
+    fi
+    # Do not actually modify config on dry run
+    [[ -z $2 ]] || continue
+    # Actually enable the component
+    $enable_func "$component"
+  done < "$1"
+
+  # Make sure to propagate the error
+  [[ -z $bad ]]
+}
+
+_bash-it-profile-list() {
+  about 'lists all profiles from the "profiles" directory'
+  _group 'lib'
+
+  echo "Available profiles:"
+  for profile in "${BASH_IT}/profiles"/*.bash_it; do
+    profile="${profile##*/}"
+    echo "${profile/.bash_it/}"
+  done
+}
+
+_bash-it-profile-rm() {
+  about 'Removes a profile from the "profiles" directory'
+  _group 'lib'
+  local name="$1"
+  if [[ -z $name ]]; then
+    echo -e "\033[91mPlease specify profile name to remove...\033[m"
+    return 1
+  fi
+
+  # Users should not be allowed to delete the default profile
+  if [[ $name == "default" ]]; then
+    echo -e "\033[91mCan not remove the default profile...\033[m"
+    return 1
+  fi
+
+  local profile_path="${BASH_IT}/profiles/$name.bash_it"
+  if [[ ! -f "$profile_path" ]]; then
+    echo -e "\033[91mCould not find profile \"$name\"...\033[m"
+    return 1
+  fi
+
+  command rm "$profile_path"
+  echo "Removed profile \"$name\" successfully!"
+}
+
+_bash-it-profile-load() {
+  _about 'loads a configuration from the "profiles" directory'
+  _group 'lib'
+
+  local name="$1"
+  if [[ -z $name ]]; then
+    echo -e "\033[91mPlease specify profile name to load, not changing configuration...\033[m"
+    return 1
+  fi
+
+  local profile_path="${BASH_IT}/profiles/$name.bash_it"
+  if [[ ! -f "$profile_path" ]]; then
+    echo -e "\033[91mCould not find profile \"$name\", not changing configuration...\033[m"
+    return 1
+  fi
+
+  echo "Trying to parse profile \"$name\"..."
+  if _bash-it-profile-load-parse-profile "$profile_path" "dry"; then
+    echo "Profile \"$name\" parsed successfully!"
+    echo "Disabling current configuration..."
+    _disable-all
+    echo ""
+    echo "Enabling configuration based on profile..."
+    _bash-it-profile-load-parse-profile "$profile_path"
+    echo ""
+    echo "Profile \"$name\" enabled!"
+  fi
+}

   _group 'lib'

+_bash-it-determine-component-status-from-path ()
+{

problem_statement:
Any method of exporting a bash-it configuration to another machine or ditfile repo?
I have been using bash-it for a week or two now and I like it a lot. Takes a lot of prior work I did myself and streamlines it. One thing I have noticed, or have not yet figured out, is how to move my personal bash-it config (including theme, active plugins, aliases, etc.) from one machine to another. My current workaround is to just make a tarball, copy it over with rsync and then untar it on the other machine. In the long term this is a problem. I looked through historic bash-it issues and didn't see any mention and I tried to look through documentation, code, and just `ls` through the bash-it dir to see if such a config file or export feature exists. 

I thought about just pointing my local bash-it at my fork of the project but that seemed less than elegant. Additionally, I would like to have some method of adding bash-it to my ditfile repo without having to use a submodule.

Any chance this issue has been tackled or there already exists a method to do what I want to do? If not, and it sounds like something that would be appreciated, I don't mind taking on the issue.

### Expected behavior

The nvm plugin should only show the node version if the current folder has a `package.json` file.
Otherwise, don't show the node version.

### Current behavior

Always shows the node version when the plugin is loaded.

### Possible solution

I don't know, but there's a similar discussion here: https://github.com/romkatv/powerlevel10k/issues/373

### Context

It just takes up extra line space when it is not relevant. E.g., working on a python project, or working on ansible.

### Notes

You guys are awesome. <3

feat: toggle off plugin repo sync
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

<!-- A clear and concise description of what the problem is. Ex. I'm always frustrated when [...] -->

The plugin repo sync ocurrs every 60 minutes and can be configured via `plugin_repository_last_check_duration`, however there is no way to turn off the sync completely.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

<!-- A clear and concise description of what you want to happen. -->

Allow `plugin_repository_last_check_duration` to be set to the special value of `never` and bypass the sync completely.

**Describe similar asdf features and why they are not sufficient**

<!-- Describe asdf features you tried to use to accomplish what you wanted. Explain why they are insufficient for the task you were trying to accomplish. -->

Setting `plugin_repository_last_check_duration` to `999999999`mins (1902 years) is an option, but not the same as completely turning off the sync.

**Describe workarounds you've considered**

<!-- A clear and concise description of any alternative solutions or features you've considered. -->

NA

**Additional context**

<!-- Add any other context or screenshots about the feature request here. -->

This was raised in https://github.com/asdf-vm/asdf/pull/957#issuecomment-865035303

I expected the configured name to take precedence, particularly because the documentation states: "Typically you should not override the default value unless you know you want asdf to ignore .tool-versions files".

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a .tool-versions file in the home directory:

```﻿﻿
erlang 24.0.6
elixir 1.12.3-otp-24
golang 1.17.2
```

2. Create a .tool-versions-foobar  file in the home directory.

```
erlang ref:master
elixir 1.12.3-otp-24
golang 1.17.2
```

3. `export ASDF_DEFAULT_TOOL_VERSIONS_FILENAME='.tool-versions-foobar'`
4. run `asdf current`

elixir          1.12.3-otp-24   /$HOME/.tool-versions-foobar

nodejs          ______          No version set. Run "asdf <global|shell|local> nodejs <version>"
rust            ______          No version set. Run "asdf <global|shell|local> rust <version>"
```

```shell

problem_statement:
Show `plugin update` path
### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe

It is not clear where `asdf` persists plugin updates.
```
$ asdf plugin update ruby
Updating ruby to master
From https://github.com/asdf-vm/asdf-ruby
   cfc5fb1..5e2eded  master     -> master
   cfc5fb1..5e2eded  master     -> origin/master
Already on 'master'
Your branch is up to date with 'origin/master'.
```

For Gitpod workflow, all changes that need to be persisted should be stored in `/workspace` - everything else is being reset on restarts, and `asdf` doesn't show where it stores updates.

### Describe the proposed solution

```
$ asdf plugin update ruby
Plugin ruby location: /whatever
Updating ruby to master
From https://github.com/asdf-vm/asdf-ruby
   cfc5fb1..5e2eded  master     -> master
   cfc5fb1..5e2eded  master     -> origin/master
Already on 'master'
Your branch is up to date with 'origin/master'.
```

### Describe similar `asdf` features and why they are not sufficient

I don't know any.

### Describe other workarounds you've considered

Can't think of UX workarounds.

problem_statement:
Add to PATH only once
I use Z Shell as both a login shell and a main shell, so `.zshrc` gets sourced twice = I get a PATH with the following contents:

```
/home/user/.asdf/bin
/home/user/.asdf/shims
/home/user/.asdf/bin
/home/user/.asdf/shims
/usr/local/sbin
/usr/local/bin
/usr/bin
```

Not a big deal functionally, but this makes it harder to parse a PATH with eyes, when, for example, troubleshooting some ordering issue. Putting `source "${HOME}/.asdf/asdf.sh"` in `.zprofile` is not an option, since `source "${HOME}/.asdf/completions/asdf.bash"`, which needs to remain in `.zshrc`, depends on it. Please, consider doing [something of this sort](https://unix.stackexchange.com/a/124447/21976).

problem_statement:
Crash when running global node command
### Steps to reproduce

install Node.js (in my tests 12.4.0):

```sh
$ asdf current
nodejs         12.4.0   (set by /Users/ushu/.tool-versions)
```

Then globally install `standard-version`:

```sh
$ npm install -f standard-version
# or with yarn (crashes the same)
$ yarn global add standard-version
```

### Expected behavior

It should run the executable, eg:

```sh
$ standard-version 
✔ outputting changes to CHANGELOG.md
✔ committing CHANGELOG.md
✔ tagging release v0.7.5
```

### Actual behavior

It crashes at line 690 of utils.sh:

```sh
$ standard-version 
/usr/local/opt/asdf/lib/utils.sh: ligne 690: executable_path: 12.4.0 : erreur de syntaxe : opérateur arithmétique non valable (le symbole erroné est « .4.0 »)
No standard-version executable found for nodejs 12.4.0
```
(sorry my shell is in French...)

From a few test, I could determine it is due to this line: https://github.com/asdf-vm/asdf/blob/master/lib/utils.sh#L690

And more precisely this expression: `"${shim_name}"`.
Since there `shim_name="standard-version"`, it seems that bash interprets the dash (`-`) in the "shim name" as a "minus operator" so it breaks everything...

### Environment

**OS**:

macOS 10.14.5 (18F96h)

```sh
Darwin IAPP-MBP-15-2014.local 18.6.0 Darwin Kernel Version 18.6.0: Thu Mar 14 21:02:45 PDT 2019; root:xnu-4903.260.65~14/RELEASE_X86_64 x86_64
```

**asdf version**:

```sh
$ asdf --version
v0.7.4
```

problem_statement:
`asdf latest` command should defer to plugin to determine latest version
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

The `asdf latest` command assumes versions listed by the `list-all` command are semantic versions. This assumption is not necessarily correct for all plugins and could cause problems.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

The `asdf latest` should invoke a plugin callback named `latest-stable` when one is present to compute the latest version. If the `latest-stable` script is missing the `asdf latest` command should fallback to computing the latest version as it does now by assuming the versions are semantic versions.

**Describe workarounds you've considered**

None. This seems to be the most straightforward solution to this problem.

**Additional context**

This is actually what was requested for https://github.com/asdf-vm/asdf/issues/216 but was never properly implemented.

* https://github.com/asdf-vm/asdf/pull/575
* https://github.com/asdf-vm/asdf/issues/216

+## `bats::on_failure` hook
+
+While `teardown` unconditionally handles cleanup after the test ends, the `bats::on_failure` hook gets called 
+only when a test is aborted due to an error. `bats::on_failure` will be called before `teardown`.
+
+You can define `bats::on_failure` anywhere in your test files, even inside the test functions, to change its behavior midtest:
+
+```bash
+@test "my awesome test" {
+  simple_test_setup
+
+  bats::on_failure() {
+    handle_simple_error_case
+  }
+
+  complex_test_setup
+
+  bats::on_failure() {
+    print_debug_information_only_on_error
+  }
+
+  do_actual_tests
+
+  check_results
+}
+```
+
+The `bats::on_failure` hook is available in `setup_suite`/`setup_file`/`setup`, their respective teardown functions, and test functions.
+

problem_statement:
Add on_failure callback
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Sometimes we want to react to test failures in a specific way, doing special cleanup, inspecting in an interactive shell, ... currently, we can only use `teardown` and check whether the test completed.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
An `on_failure` callback function that gets called immediately, when the test is known to have failed. As a bonus this might allow for overriding the failure.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Special "failure only" cleanup can be done in `teardown` but is a bit more cumbersome. Dropping into an interactive shell could be solved with a specialized flag.

problem_statement:
Out of band deprecation warnings
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Future version of Bats might deprecate features and should warn users about this.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Bats could collect all deprecation warnings of a run in `$BATS_RUN_TMPDIR/warnings.log`. Obviously, the log should contain the call site that triggered the warning and a short explanation. The log should be printed to stderr after all test results have been reported.

 Longer explanations might be put into documentation or the wiki like shellcheck does.
Similarly, we might want to allow for disabling these warnings locally/globally.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Instead of using a file, we could insert the deprecation warnings into the normal test output. However, this would hide them on successful tests and they might drown between the other outputs.

**Additional context**
Candidates for future deprecation:
- unprefixed functions like `load`, `run`, `skip`...

problem_statement:
Extended tap formatter gets confused when retrying  tests
Hello everyone!

Thanks for this excellent and useful project!

**Describe the bug**
A clear and concise description of what the bug is.
I believe I found a bug when in the extended tap parser that gets triggered when tests are re-tried (with the recently introduced `BATS_TEST_RETRIES` feature).

**To Reproduce**

Test file:

```sh
#!/usr/bin/env bats

BATS_TEST_RETRIES=1

@test "test foobar" {
  echo "Hello, world!"
  exit 1
}
```

Run with `bats -p test-file.bats`.

Observe strange `begin 1` or `begin 2` output in front of the test name.

```sh
# bats -F pretty test-file.bats 
test-file.bats
[1/1]   test foobar
2 begin 1 test foobar
[2/1]   begin 1 test foobar
 ✗
   (in test file test-file.bats, line 7)
     `exit 1' failed
   Hello, world!

1 test, 1 failure
```

**Expected behavior**
All extended formatters should handle retried tests correctly.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - Bats Version: 1.9.0
 - OS: Alma 9 Linux
 - Bash version: 5.1.8

**Additional context**
Add any other context about the problem here.

I believe the issue is coming from this line: https://github.com/bats-core/bats-core/blob/e4ddb10402d9df809396938f48b36ae73d10dcd6/lib/bats-core/formatter.bash#L54

Basically, the parser assumes that `begin_index` will always match `index` (and thus can be used to strip off the number from the line). However, this is not the case for retried tests, since bats does not increment the `index` for each test retry, but `begin_index` is incremented for each `begin` tap line.

This can be seen based on the following `--formatter cat` output (where the test `If namespace has no label then route will get external-dns annotation pointing to default router shard` was retried twice (and failed twice).

```sh
# bats -F cat test-file.bats 
1..1
suite /okd4-install/test-file.bats
begin 1 test foobar
begin 1 test foobar
not ok 1 test foobar
# (in test file test-file.bats, line 7)
#   `exit 1' failed
# Hello, world!
```

https://github.com/docker-mailserver/docker-mailserver/blob/7293e3c9e8fed5020495f0bbfc8805e3a7fe3683/target/scripts/startup/setup-stack.sh#L1624

I bet a check could be added to avoid the chmod +x on each run

chmod: changing permissions of '/tmp/docker-mailserver/user-patches.sh': Read-only file system
```

I mount as read only the script `- ${USER_PATCHES_FILE:-./user-patches.sh}:/tmp/docker-mailserver/user-patches.sh:ro`

```

```Markdown
1. /etc/cron.d/amavisd-new don`t work
2. description in the documentation about mandatory creation of an alias for internal users
For example `./setup.sh alias add @mail.example.com postmaster@example.com`
```

```Markdown
1. deploy container with ENABLE_AMAVIS=0

@@ -91,3 +91,40 @@ function _vhost_ldap_support() {
 #
 # /etc/aliases is handled by `alias.sh` and uses `postalias` to update the Postfix alias database. No need for `postmap`.
 # http://www.postfix.org/postalias.1.html
+
+# Add an key with an value to Postfix's main configuration file
+# or update an existing key. An already existing key can be updated
+# by either appending to the existing value (default) or by prepending.
+#
+# @param ${1} = key name in Postfix's main configuration file
+# @param ${2} = new value (appended or prepended)
+# @param ${3} = "append" (default) or "prepend" [OPTIONAL]
+function _add_to_or_update_postfix_main() {
+  local KEY=${1:?Key name is required}
+  local NEW_VALUE=${2:?New value is required}
+  local ACTION=${3:-append}
+
+  # If entry does not exist, add it - otherwise update with ACTION:
+  if ! grep -q -E "^${KEY}" /etc/postfix/main.cf; then
+    postconf "${KEY} = ${NEW_VALUE}"
+  else
+    KEY=$(_escape_for_sed "${KEY}")
+    NEW_VALUE=$(_escape_for_sed "${NEW_VALUE}")
+    local SED_STRING
+
+    case "${ACTION}" in
+      ('append')
+        SED_STRING="/${NEW_VALUE}/! s|^(${KEY} *=.*)|\1 ${NEW_VALUE}|g"
+        ;;
+      ('prepend')
+        SED_STRING="/${NEW_VALUE}/! s|^(${KEY}) *= *(.*)|\1 = ${NEW_VALUE} \2|g"
+        ;;
+      (*)
+        _log 'error' "Action '${3}' in _add_to_or_update_postfix_main is unknown"
+        return 1
+        ;;
+    esac
+
+    sed -i -E "${SED_STRING}" /etc/postfix/main.cf
+  fi
+}

problem_statement: bug report: Postfix `main.cf:smtpd_milters` appends `$rspamd_milter` on restarts ### 📝 Preliminary Checks - [X] I tried searching for an existing issue and followed the [debugging docs](https://docker-mailserver.github.io/docker-mailserver/latest/config/debugging/) advice, but still need assistance. ### 👀 What Happened? A [user has identified a bug](https://github.com/orgs/docker-mailserver/discussions/3481#discussioncomment-6720861) similar to one recently resolved by https://github.com/docker-mailserver/docker-mailserver/pull/3380 where a setting is updated by appending a value, but repeated restarts do not check if it was already appended (_internal config is expected to be deterministic at startup, not modified from prior restart_). https://github.com/docker-mailserver/docker-mailserver/blob/8f971713360c4620046c7f223fe66df9ea800253/target/scripts/startup/setup.d/security/rspamd.sh#L141 This `sed` approach has been used a fair bit and may result in similar bugs elsewhere. --- ### Internal state persisting across restarts is a known concern This isn't too surprising; maintainers are well aware of DMS not playing well with restarts. We've given explicit advice in many issues to [properly restart DMS](https://github.com/docker-mailserver/docker-mailserver/issues/3462#issuecomment-1669120153) via either: - `docker compose down` (_`ctrl +c` alone is not equivalent_) + `docker compose up` - `docker compose up --force-recreate` (_no `down` command required_). Our docs also try raise awareness in [Usage guide](https://docker-mailserver.github.io/docker-mailserver/v12.1/usage/#get-up-and-running) (_perhaps should also mention in [Debugging docs](https://docker-mailserver.github.io/docker-mailserver/v12.1/config/debugging/)_): Internal configs being changed may not be deterministic with current scripts otherwise. While this approach won't help if any volume mounted configs (_that aren't copied internally_) were modified by DMS, but we tend to have less assumptions by scripts in those cases to avoid the problem. ### 👟 Reproduction Steps _No response_ ### 🐋 DMS Version 12.1 / edge ### 💻 Operating System and Architecture N/A ### ⚙️ Container configuration files _No response_ ### 📜 Relevant log output _No response_ ### Improvements to this form? _No response_

problem_statement:
feature request: Idle load - ``check-for-changes.sh`` improve execution interval
### Context

I noticed that amongst other container docker-mailservers has an unusal high idle load on my machine.

While debugging the running process I saw that ``check-for-changes.sh`` causes roughly ~50% of the idle load

Note: ``ENABLE_RSPAMD`` is set to 1

### Description

``check-for-changes.sh`` checks every 2 seconds for changes:

https://github.com/docker-mailserver/docker-mailserver/blob/6b1a5664979528064672f056bf0dd8fe0c421952/target/scripts/check-for-changes.sh#L213-L214

As described above this causes a lot of idle load.

The check invokes 

https://github.com/docker-mailserver/docker-mailserver/blob/6b1a5664979528064672f056bf0dd8fe0c421952/target/scripts/check-for-changes.sh#L37-L60

and this executes

https://github.com/docker-mailserver/docker-mailserver/blob/6b1a5664979528064672f056bf0dd8fe0c421952/target/scripts/helpers/change-detection.sh#L24-L80

As far as I can tell these extremely frequent checks are likely only required when debugging/actively changing configuration files.

I therefore propose the following:
1. Make the change interval configurable (e.g. using a env variable like ``CHECK_FOR_CHANGES_INTERVAL_SEC``)
2. Change the default interval sec to something higher like ``5`` or ``10`` to lessen the default idle load
3. Document this somewhere 
    * Recommend lower values during active development/configuration and higher ones when not

### Alternatives

N/A

### Applicable Users

Everyone

### Are you going to implement it?

+# Postfix resolves `virtual_alias_maps` before `virtual_mailbox_maps`. A catch-all alias (`@example.com`)
+# therefore also captures mail for the accounts of that domain, unless each account is an alias to itself.
+# https://github.com/docker-mailserver/docker-mailserver/issues/4856

+# These identity aliases are only written to `/etc/postfix/virtual` and never to `postfix-virtual.cf`:
+# - `setup alias add` rejects them on purpose (an alias and account sharing an address caused forwarding problems).
+# - Quota dummy accounts (`accounts.sh:_create_dovecot_alias_dummy_accounts`) and `setup alias list` stay unaffected.
+#
+# An account that is explicitly listed in `postfix-virtual.cf` keeps the entry of the user.
+# NOTE: Expects `/etc/postfix/virtual` to be a fresh copy of `postfix-virtual.cf` (see `_handle_postfix_virtual_config`).
+function __add_identity_aliases_for_catch_all_domains() {
+  local DATABASE_ACCOUNTS='/tmp/docker-mailserver/postfix-accounts.cf'
+  local DATABASE_VIRTUAL='/tmp/docker-mailserver/postfix-virtual.cf'
+
+  # LDAP does not use `postfix-accounts.cf`, a stale file must not change how its catch-all behaves:
+  [[ ${ACCOUNT_PROVISIONER} == 'FILE' ]] || return 0
+  [[ -f ${DATABASE_ACCOUNTS} ]] || return 0
+
+  # The copy might lack a final newline, which would merge the first appended line into the last one:
+  _append_final_newline_if_missing /etc/postfix/virtual
+
+  # A single `awk` pass over both files is the upgrade path should this become noticeable at startup.
+  local MAIL_ACCOUNT
+  while IFS='|' read -r MAIL_ACCOUNT _; do
+    if _db_has_entry_with_key "@${MAIL_ACCOUNT#*@}" "${DATABASE_VIRTUAL}" \
+    && ! _db_has_entry_with_key "${MAIL_ACCOUNT}" "${DATABASE_VIRTUAL}"; then
+      _log 'debug' "Adding identity alias for '${MAIL_ACCOUNT}' as its domain has a catch-all alias"
+      echo "${MAIL_ACCOUNT} ${MAIL_ACCOUNT}" >>/etc/postfix/virtual
+    fi
+  done < <(_get_valid_lines_from_file "${DATABASE_ACCOUNTS}")
+}

problem_statement:
bug: mailboxes cannot be added via `setup` on a domain with a catch-all alias
### 📝 Preliminary Checks

- [x] I tried searching for an existing issue and followed the [debugging docs](https://docker-mailserver.github.io/docker-mailserver/latest/config/debugging/) advice, but still need assistance.
- [x] I will disclose any AI assistance I have used with the information I provide in my report, so that I do not waste the time of humans trying to help me.

### 👀 What Happened?

### Summary

On a domain with a catch-all alias, DMS's own CLI cannot create a working mailbox. The workaround recommended by maintainers (self-alias `addr -> addr`) is rejected by `setup` since v12.1 (#3270). Users are pointed to #3022, which has been dormant since 2023 – yet it was still referenced as "the place to follow" in #4594 (Oct 2025).

### Steps to reproduce

1. `postfix-virtual.cf` contains a catch-all:
   ```
   @example.com someone@example.com
   ```
2. Add a mailbox:
   ```console
   setup email add new@example.com
   ```
3. Add the self-alias required for the catch-all (as recommended in #3022 and the docs):
   ```console
   $ setup alias add new@example.com new@example.com
   ERROR addalias: 'new@example.com' is already defined as an account
   ERROR addalias: Aborting
   ```
   The reverse order fails as well:
   ```console
   $ setup email add new@example.com
   ERROR addmailuser: 'new@example.com' is already defined as an alias
   ERROR addmailuser: Aborting
   ```

### Actual behavior

The account is created, but all mail to it is **silently** delivered to the catch-all target – no bounce, no warning. The only fix is editing `postfix-virtual.cf` by hand, i.e. bypassing the CLI guard.

### Expected behavior

Adding a mailbox with `setup` results in a mailbox that actually receives mail.

### Why this is a bug, not a feature request

- The docs state that with a catch-all *"you will need an alias for each non-alias address of that domain"*.
- #3022 recommends exactly this self-alias workaround. A reporter there hit the same error (`'blackhole@example.com' is already defined as an account`) – never answered.
- #4594 (Oct 2025) confirms the setup works when edited manually, but calls it "unsupported".

So the documented and recommended configuration **cannot be produced with the supported tooling**. This affects every mailbox added to a domain after a catch-all exists.

### Proposed fix (smallest first)

1. Exempt the identity mapping (`addr -> addr`) from the overlap check in `addalias`. It cannot cause the forwarding/ARC problems the guard was introduced for (#3350, #4400).
2. Or: let `setup email add` create the self-alias automatically when a catch-all exists for that domain – at the very least print a warning that the new account will be swallowed by the catch-all.
3. Long term: resolve #3022 so a catch-all no longer requires dummy aliases at all.

### Environment

- DMS version: `v17.0.0`
- Related: #3022, #3270, #3350, #4400, #4594

## AI disclosure

This report was drafted with the help of an AI assistant (Claude). The error messages and the behavior (catch-all swallowing mail for a new account, `setup` rejecting both orders) were reproduced and verified by me on my own DMS instance. References to #3022, #3350, #4400 and #4594 were checked manually.

_No response_

v17.0.0

### 💻 Operating System and Architecture

Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS

```yml

```

Bashmarks Issues Saving Directories
Upon installation, the bashmarks plugin has been behaving incorrectly in strange ways; strange enough that actually showing the behavior will be much easier than attempting to use prose exclusively.

In the following screenshot, bashmarks begins with no bookmarks. As is demonstrated, when bashmarks has one or more bookmarks saved, a `cannot overwrite existing file` message is shown.

![ohmybash oh-my-bash 01](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/20735042/56549282-99d92280-653f-11e9-8f49-df6550d8492d.png)

Attempting as best I can to describe the incorrect behavior observed:

  1. A `cannot overwrite existing file` error message is shown when saving a 
     bookmark with one or more existing bookmarks.
  2. The `home` bookmark is either never saved, or is deleted for an unknown
     reason.
  3. After saving `home` for the second time, the behavior seems to normalize,
     sauf the aforementioned error message.

There are however, more issues. I've encountered another after starting a new instance of bash; this time the `media` bookmark is deleted.

![ohmybash oh-my-bash 02](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/20735042/56549954-7c0cbd00-6541-11e9-8e19-2b3fd68c2bc0.png)

Based on these observations, it seems that the issue is related to the implementation of bookmark saving, especially that involving the temporary files (`/tmp/bashmarks.6oXbma`, `/tmp/bashmarks.kJ0zFh`, et cetera, in the examples provided).

+#! bash oh-my-bash.module
+# Copyright 2023 Koichi Murase.
+#
+# Helper functions for completions
+#
+
+## @fn _omb_completion_reassemble_breaks exclude
+##   @param[in] $1 exclude Characters to exclude from COMP_WORDSBREAKS
+##   @var[out] cur[0] Current word after reassembly
+##   @var[out] cur[1] Part of ${cur[0]} that was originally in previous words
+##     in COMP_WORDS.
+##   @arr[out] COMPREPLY This functions empties the array COMPREPLY.
+function _omb_completion_reassemble_breaks {
+  local exclude=$1
+  local line=$COMP_LINE point=$COMP_POINT
+  local breaks=${COMP_WORDBREAKS//[\"\'$exclude]}
+
+  COMPREPLY=()
+  cur=("${COMP_WORDS[COMP_CWORD]}" '')
+
+  local word rprefix= rword=
+  for word in "${COMP_WORDS[@]::COMP_CWORD+1}"; do
+    local space=${line%%"$word"*}
+    if [[ $space == "$line" ]]; then
+      # error: COMP_LINE does not contain enough words
+      return 1
+    fi
+
+    word=${word::point - ${#space}}
+    if [[ $space || $rword == *["$breaks"] || $word == ["$breaks"]* ]]; then
+      rprefix=
+      rword=$word
+    else
+      rprefix=$rword
+      rword+=$word
+    fi
+
+    line=${line:${#space}+${#word}}
+    ((point -= ${#space} + ${#word}))
+    ((point >= 0)) || break
+  done
+
+  cur=("$rword" "$rprefix")
+}
+
+## @fn _omb_completion_resolve_breaks
+##   Adjust completions generated for the reassembled word
+##   @var[out] cur[1] Prefix to remove set by _omb_completion_reassemble_breaks
+##   @arr[out] COMPREPLY This functions empties the array COMPREPLY.
+function _omb_completion_resolve_breaks {
+  if [[ ${cur[1]} ]]; then
+    local i
+    for i in "${!COMPREPLY[@]}"; do
+      if [[ ${COMPREPLY[i]} == "$cur_prefix"* ]]; then
+        COMPREPLY[i]=${COMPREPLY[i]#"$cur_prefix"}
+      else
+        unset -v 'COMPREPLY[i]'
+      fi
+    done
+    COMPREPLY=("${COMPREPLY[@]}")
+  fi
+}

problem_statement:
emacsclient.sh makes assumptions on emacs output that don't hold ### Describe the bug Using the `emacs` plugin, which adds an `e` alias, which calls `oh-my-zsh/plugins/emacs/emacsclient.sh`. Logic in that script: You call it with a file to be opened in emacs. 1. use the system's `emacsclient` to execute a bit of list that lists all active frames (i.e., what you'd call "window" in a modern GUI) 2. if there's empty string or `nil` returned, create a new frame, so show a new (X11/windows/…) window
if there's none, display in current frame Sadly, the check fails: if you add a few debug `echos`, you'll get something funky happening: ```shell # Only create another X frame if there isn't one present if [ -z "${frames}" -o "${frames}" = 'nil' ]; then echo "frames ($frames) evaluated empty or nil" emacsclient --alternate-editor "" --create-frame "$@" return $? fi echo "frames ($frames) evaluated non-nil, no new frame" emacsclient --alternate-editor "" "$@" ``` which then happily proceeds to tell us, at least when run without an emacs daemon already running, ```text frames (nil) evaluated non-nil, no new frame ``` Well, I was flabbergasted, `nil != nil`? And on the second run, suddenly `nil = nil`! Turns out, when you hexdump the non-nil `nil`, i.e., the one that emacs spits out on the second (and subsequent) run, there's a bunch of invisible characters being printed. ```text 00000000: 1b5d 3132 3b23 6666 6666 6666 6666 3030 .]12;#ffffffff00 00000010: 3030 076e 696c 0a 00.nil. ``` So, this is an unlucky combination of emacs (with plugins, but who uses vanilla emacs?) in modern versions starting some kind of TUI without much ado, which already prints something, only to be then *followed* by something printable, namely the contents we instructed to get via lisp. ### Steps to reproduce 1. enable plugin `emacs` 2. (make sure no emacs daemon is running.) Run `e ~/.zshrc` 3. Instead of starting emacs, opening a new GUI window and opening .zshrc in that, you get a quickly popping up terminal-mode emacs (which you did not request), which instantly closes again ### Expected behavior 1. enable plugin `emacs` 2. (make sure no emacs daemon is running.) Run `e ~/.zshrc` 3. opens a new GUI window and .zshrc in that ### Screenshots and recordings _No response_ ### OS / Linux distribution Fedora 36 Linux, ### Zsh version 5.8.1 ### Oh My Zsh version master (50550c70) ### Terminal emulator alacritty ### If using WSL on Windows, which version of WSL _No response_ ### Additional context A solution could either be 1. fix the lisp command passed to emacsclient to list frames: `(delete 't (mapcar 'framep (frame-list)))` to instead pipe the result into a (temporary) file. Read that file instead of stdout. 2. Strip all characters up to and including the 0x07 byte (ASCII Bell symbol) in the `$frames` string If I knew enough lisp to make this not only work, but work *reliable* across platforms, I'd go for 1. Alas, I don't. So, `frames="$(emacsclient -a '' -n -e "$cmd" 2>/dev/null |sed 's/.*\x07//g' )"` it is for me for now, but it's a dirty hotfix.

problem_statement:
Inconsistent `ls` alias, new window vs. omz reload; overwrites `alias ls='gls --color=tty'` only on reload
### Describe the bug

relevant info:

- os: macOS `13.3.1`
- arch: `arm64`
- terminal application: iTerm2 3.5.0beta10
- shell: zsh 5.9, `/bin/zsh` (macOS built-in version)
- special config: using ["typewritten"](https://typewritten.dev) theme
- plugins: occurs with or without any plugins

---

Opening a new window vs. using `omz reload` (or entering the debug session with `zsh -xv 2> >(tee ~/omz-debug.log &>/dev/null)`, for that matter) creates inconsistent `ls` alias:

**new terminal window/tab**
```sh
> type -a ls
ls is an alias for ls -G
ls is /bin/ls
```

**after `omz reload`, `zsh`, `tmux` etc.**
```sh
> type -a ls
ls is an alias for gls --color=tty
ls is /bin/ls
```

this is problematic (at least on macOS) since there are several `ls` flags (such as `ls -@` which shows extended attributes) that result in error with `gls`.

I'm pretty sure the culprit is in [`lib/theme-and-appearance`,  lines 48-57](https://github.com/ohmyzsh/ohmyzsh/blob/5d3e86e2a48adf7a308773f8f1b725d187c7c5ef/lib/theme-and-appearance.zsh#L48-L57):
```sh
  (darwin|freebsd)*)
    # This alias works by default just using $LSCOLORS
    test-ls-args ls -G && alias ls='ls -G'
    # Only use GNU ls if installed and there are user defaults for $LS_COLORS,
    # as the default coloring scheme is not very pretty
    [[ -n "$LS_COLORS" || -f "$HOME/.dircolors" ]] \
      && test-ls-args gls --color \
      && alias ls='gls --color=tty'
    ;;
  *)
```

NOTE: this does **not** occur when `DISABLE_LS_COLORS="true"`

why does this seem to run after invoking `zsh` but _not_ when `zsh` is initialized for a new window/tab?
it would be cool if there were a flag to turn off overwriting of builtin commands with coreutils variants _but still be able to have nice LS\_COLORS_

### Steps to reproduce

1. open a new terminal
2. run `which ls` or `type -a ls` or whatever
3. note the result
4. run any of the following: `omz reload`, `exec zsh`, `zsh`, `tmux`, `asciinema`
5. note that now `ls is an alias for gls --color=tty`

### Expected behavior

either `type -a ls` should be consistent with new window / omz reload OR ideally `gls` wouldn't be used by default on macOS for the reason that `gls` is missing some features unique to the macOS implementation (e.g. `-@`)

### Screenshots and recordings

unfortunately, it's impossible to reproduce this using `asciinema` because it runs a new `zsh` instance and so the `gls` alias is already used. here is a regular-ass video

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8978069/234725142-bef44c40-cf09-4a36-8a58-a14d8f778ed8.mp4

### workaround

manually set in `.zshrc` before `source ${OMZ}/oh-my-zsh.sh` (`LS_COLORS` might be different on your system)
```sh
export LS_COLORS="di=1;36:ln=35:so=32:pi=33:ex=31:bd=34;46:cd=34;43:su=30;41:sg=30;46:tw=30;42:ow=30;43"
alias ls='ls -G'
DISABLE_LS_COLORS="true"
```

### OS / Linux distribution

macOS 13.3.1

### Zsh version

5.9

### Oh My Zsh version

master (5d3e86e)

### Terminal emulator

iTerm2 3.5.0beta10

### If using WSL on Windows, which version of WSL

None

### Additional context

using theme `typewritten` but doesn't seem to interfere.

problem_statement:
Conventional commit aliases from `git-commit` plugin fail due to non POSIX syntax
### Describe the bug

[Git uses `sh` as its default shell, with no possibility to change it.](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/73162225/how-to-make-bash-as-default-shell-in-git-alias)

The recently created `git-commit` plugin for conventional commits adds git aliases which contain `[[` to check for conditions.
[This is non POSIX syntax](https://askubuntu.com/a/1277981) that `sh` does not recognise (but `bash` and `zsh` do.) One should use `[` instead when working with `sh`.

Offending line in the plugin:
https://github.com/ohmyzsh/ohmyzsh/blob/079dbff2c4f22935a71101c511e2285327d8ab68/plugins/git-commit/git-commit.plugin.zsh#L3


### Steps to reproduce

1. Add the plugin `plugins+=(git-commit)`
2. Reload with `omz reload`
3. `cd` into a git repository
4. Run an alias: `git feat --scope "zshrc/git-commit" "add plugin for conventional commits"`
5. Error: `error: pathspec 'something' did not match any file(s) known to git`

### Expected behavior

The alias should work properly.

### Screenshots and recordings


Terminal output:
```zsh
$ git feat --scope "zshrc/git-commit" "add plugin for conventional commits"
a() { if [[ "$1" == "-s" || "$1" == "--scope" ]]; then git commit -m "feat(${2}): ${@:3}"; else git commit -m "feat: ${@}"; fi }; a: 1: [[: not found
a() { if [[ "$1" == "-s" || "$1" == "--scope" ]]; then git commit -m "feat(${2}): ${@:3}"; else git commit -m "feat: ${@}"; fi }; a: 1: --scope: not found
error: pathspec 'zshrc/git-commit' did not match any file(s) known to git
error: pathspec 'add plugin for conventional commits' did not match any file(s) known to git
```

### OS / Linux distribution

Ubuntu 20.04

### Zsh version

5.8

### Oh My Zsh version

master (079dbff)

### Terminal emulator

Windows Terminal (1.17.11461.0)

### If using WSL on Windows, which version of WSL

WSL2

### Additional context

I suspect that the creator of this plugin set up a symlink to point `sh` to `bash` on their machine and didn't realise that this was not the default for most people. Will open a PR to fix it.

diff --git a/lib/async_prompt.zsh b/lib/async_prompt.zsh
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000000..c6d03328b16f4
--- /dev/null
+++ b/lib/async_prompt.zsh
@@ -0,0 +1,140 @@
+# The async code is taken from
+# https://github.com/zsh-users/zsh-autosuggestions/blob/master/src/async.zsh
+# https://github.com/woefe/git-prompt.zsh/blob/master/git-prompt.zsh
+
+zmodload zsh/system
+
+# For now, async prompt function handlers are set up like so:
+# First, define the async function handler and add the function name
+# to the _omz_async_functions array:
+#
+#  function _git_prompt_status_async {
+#    # Do some expensive operation that outputs to stdout
+#  }
+#  _omz_register_handler _git_prompt_status_async
+#
+# Then add a stub prompt function in `$PROMPT` or similar prompt variables,
+# which will show the output of "$_OMZ_ASYNC_OUTPUT[handler_name]":
+#
+#  function git_prompt_status {
+#    echo -n $_OMZ_ASYNC_OUTPUT[_git_prompt_status]
+#  }
+#
+#  RPROMPT='$(git_prompt_status)'
+#
+# This API is subject to change and optimization. Rely on it at your own risk.
+
+function _omz_register_handler {
+  setopt localoptions noksharrays
+  typeset -ga _omz_async_functions
+  # we want to do nothing if there's no $1 function or we already set it up
+  if [[ -z "$1" ]] || (( ! ${+functions[$1]} )) \
+    || (( ${_omz_async_functions[(Ie)$1]} )); then
+    return
+  fi
+  _omz_async_functions+=("$1")
+  # let's add the hook to async_request if it's not there yet
+  if (( ! ${precmd_functions[(Ie)_omz_async_request]} )) \
+    && (( ${+functions[_omz_async_request]})); then
+    autoload -Uz add-zsh-hook
+    add-zsh-hook precmd _omz_async_request
+  fi
+}
+
+# Set up async handlers and callbacks
+function _omz_async_request {
+  typeset -gA _OMZ_ASYNC_FDS _OMZ_ASYNC_PIDS _OMZ_ASYNC_OUTPUT
+
+  # executor runs a subshell for all async requests based on key
+  local handler
+  for handler in ${_omz_async_functions}; do
+    (( ${+functions[$handler]} )) || continue
+
+    local fd=${_OMZ_ASYNC_FDS[$handler]:--1}
+    local pid=${_OMZ_ASYNC_PIDS[$handler]:--1}
+
+    # If we've got a pending request, cancel it
+    if (( fd != -1 && pid != -1 )) && { true <&$fd } 2>/dev/null; then
+      # Close the file descriptor and remove the handler
+      exec {fd}<&-
+      zle -F $fd
+
+      # Zsh will make a new process group for the child process only if job
+      # control is enabled (MONITOR option)
+      if [[ -o MONITOR ]]; then
+        # Send the signal to the process group to kill any processes that may
+        # have been forked by the async function handler
+        kill -TERM -$pid 2>/dev/null
+      else
+        # Kill just the child process since it wasn't placed in a new process
+        # group. If the async function handler forked any child processes they may
+        # be orphaned and left behind.
+        kill -TERM $pid 2>/dev/null
+      fi
+    fi
+
+    # Define global variables to store the file descriptor, PID and output
+    _OMZ_ASYNC_FDS[$handler]=-1
+    _OMZ_ASYNC_PIDS[$handler]=-1
+
+    # Fork a process to fetch the git status and open a pipe to read from it
+    exec {fd}< <(
+      # Tell parent process our PID
+      builtin echo ${sysparams[pid]}
+      # Store handler name for callback
+      builtin echo $handler
+      # Run the async function handler
+      $handler
+    )
+
+    # Save FD for handler
+    _OMZ_ASYNC_FDS[$handler]=$fd
+
+    # There's a weird bug here where ^C stops working unless we force a fork
+    # See https://github.com/zsh-users/zsh-autosuggestions/issues/364
+    command true
+
+    # Save the PID from the handler child process
+    read pid <&$fd
+    _OMZ_ASYNC_PIDS[$handler]=$pid
+
+    # When the fd is readable, call the response handler
+    zle -F "$fd" _omz_async_callback
+  done
+}
+
+# Called when new data is ready to be read from the pipe
+function _omz_async_callback() {
+  emulate -L zsh
+
+  local fd=$1   # First arg will be fd ready for reading
+  local err=$2  # Second arg will be passed in case of error
+
+  if [[ -z "$err" || "$err" == "hup" ]]; then
+    # Get handler name from first line
+    local handler
+    read handler <&$fd
+
+    # Store old output which is supposed to be already printed
+    local old_output="${_OMZ_ASYNC_OUTPUT[$handler]}"
+
+    # Read output from fd
+    _OMZ_ASYNC_OUTPUT[$handler]="$(cat <&$fd)"
+
+    # Repaint prompt if output has changed
+    if [[ "$old_output" != "${_OMZ_ASYNC_OUTPUT[$handler]}" ]]; then
+      zle reset-prompt
+      zle -R
+    fi
+
+    # Close the fd
+    exec {fd}<&-
+  fi
+
+  # Always remove the handler
+  zle -F "$fd"
+
+  # Unset global FD variable to prevent closing user created FDs in the precmd hook
+  _OMZ_ASYNC_FDS[$handler]=-1
+  _OMZ_ASYNC_PIDS[$handler]=-1
+}

+#!/usr/bin/env zsh
+

+emulate -L zsh
+setopt err_return
+zmodload zsh/zpty
+zmodload zsh/zselect
+

+export GLOBALIAS_TEST_RESULT=$test_dir/result
+
+wait_for_marker() {
+  local marker=$1 output received
+  local -i deadline=$(( SECONDS + 5 ))
+  while (( SECONDS < deadline )); do
+    if zpty -r globalias-test output; then
+      received+=$output
+      [[ $received == *$marker* ]] && return 0
+    else
+      zselect -t 1 || true
+    fi
+  done
+  print -u2 -r -- "Timed out waiting for ZLE: $received"
+  return 1
+}
+
+check_expansion() {
+  local input=$1 expected=$2 actual

+    print -u2 -r -- "Input: ${(qqq)input}"

+    return 1
+  fi
+}

+alias ll='ls -l'
+alias -g G='| grep'
+GLOBALIAS_FILTER_VALUES=(ll)
+_globalias_test_capture() {
+  print -rn -- "$BUFFER" > "$GLOBALIAS_TEST_RESULT"
+  print -r -- $'\nGLOBALIAS_TEST_CAPTURED'
+  BUFFER=
+  zle .accept-line
+}
+zle -N _globalias_test_capture
+bindkey '^X' _globalias_test_capture
+PS1='GLOBALIAS_TEST_READY> '
+RPROMPT=

+  zpty -w globalias-test "source ${(q)test_dir}/setup.zsh"
+  wait_for_marker GLOBALIAS_TEST_READY

+  check_expansion 'DEBUG="1"' 'DEBUG="1" '
+  check_expansion "DEBUG='1'" "DEBUG='1' "
+  check_expansion '1' 'cd -1 '
+  check_expansion '"1"' '"1" '
+  check_expansion "'1'" "'1' "
+  check_expansion '\1' '\1 '
+  check_expansion 'echo G' 'echo | grep '
+  check_expansion 'DEBUG=1 1' 'DEBUG=1 cd -1 '
+  check_expansion 'll' 'll '
+  check_expansion 'echo $((1+2))' 'echo 3 '
+  check_expansion 'echo {a,b}' 'echo a b  '
+  check_expansion '' ' '

problem_statement:
Error on zsh startup (related to ~/.profile)
After a recent upgrade of oh-my-zsh, I get the following error on OS X:

```
/usr/local/etc/autojump.bash:13: command not found: complete
/usr/local/etc/autojump.bash:52: = not found
/usr/local/etc/bash_completion:59: command not found: shopt
/usr/local/etc/bash_completion:65: command not found: complete
(more error messages here)
```

The problem appears to be that tools/check_for_upgrade.sh is now sourcing `~/.profile`:

```
[ -f ~/.profile ] && source ~/.profile
```

In my case, that files contains lines such as:

```
if [ -f `brew --prefix`/etc/autojump.bash ]; then
  . `brew --prefix`/etc/autojump.bash
fi
. /usr/local/etc/bash_completion
```

If I comment out the line check_for_upgrade.sh, the error messages go away.

Should ~/.profile be sourced (indirectly) from ~/.zshrc?
I'm not sure this is a bug, so bear with me for a minute here.

The default template for ~/.zshrc includes oh-my-zsh.sh, which in turn calls tools/check_for_upgrade.sh, which sources ~/.profile. This means that for every terminal that gets created, ~/.profile is called.

However, in my understanding (see e.g. [1](http://www.tldp.org/LDP/Bash-Beginners-Guide/html/sect_03_01.html), [2](http://serverfault.com/a/261807/112267), [3](http://mywiki.wooledge.org/DotFiles)), ~/.profile should only be executed once, on login, while ~/.zshrc is called each time a terminal window is created.

In my case concretely, this causes a problem as my ~/.profile calls xmodmap (I'm trying to configure my caps lock key as an extra backspace as per [1](http://askubuntu.com/a/82734/4335)), which doesn't like being called multiple times. In general, this might cause problems if ~/.profile contains long-running processes or code that assumes it will only be called on login.

So, to summarize: should ~/.profile be sourced in tools/check_for_upgrade.sh, and therefore be called for each terminal window that is created?

Additional info: I also tried to find out where the line sourcing ~./profile got introduced, it was added in [this commit](https://github.com/robbyrussell/oh-my-zsh/commit/a9e1d9aa890c18ea3c3250442e7d9de555633237). I dug a bit deeper to find out why it was added, which lead to [this commit](https://github.com/n-st/oh-my-zsh/commit/3f44f51e9ca1b196e4c3caa439558996abdac273), with commit message "source ~/.profile for upgrading (to source the proxy configuration)".

problem_statement:
Bug: sdk offline reaches out to api.sdkman.io.
**Bug report**

Running the command `sdk offline` or `sdk offline enable` results in unexpected network traffic. Specifically, a DNS lookup of api.sdkman.io and a bunch of HTTPS traffic to api.sdkman.io.

I'm not sure why `offline` is calling the sdkman API. This is particularly annoying when I'm partially online but have insanely slow DNS resolution. This means my shell sits waiting for sdkman's phone-home ritual even though I explicitly told it not to.

**To reproduce**

1. Start tcpdump
2. Run `sdk offline`
3. Observe traffic to api.sdkman.io

**System info**
sdkman 5.20 on Fedora: 

```
SDKMAN!
script: 5.20.0
native: 0.1.3
```

--- a/src/main/bash/sdkman-env.sh
+++ b/src/main/bash/sdkman-env.sh
@@ -18,14 +18,18 @@

 	local -r sdkmanrc=".sdkmanrc"
-	local -r sub_command="$1"
+	local -r subcommand="$1"
 
-	if [[ "$sub_command" == "init" ]]; then
-		__sdkman_generate_sdkmanrc "$sdkmanrc"
-
-		return 0
-	fi
+	case $subcommand in
+		"")    __sdkman_load_env "$sdkmanrc" ;;
+		init)  __sdkman_create_env_file "$sdkmanrc";;
+		clear) __sdkman_clear_env "$sdkmanrc";;
+	esac
+}
 
+function __sdkman_load_env() {
+	local sdkmanrc="$1"
+	
 	if [[ ! -f "$sdkmanrc" ]]; then
 		__sdkman_echo_red "Could not find $sdkmanrc in the current directory."
 		echo ""
@@ -34,6 +38,68 @@ function __sdk_env() {
 		return 1

+	__sdkman_env_each_candidate "$sdkmanrc" "__sdk_use" && 
+		SDKMAN_ENV=$PWD

+function __sdkman_create_env_file() {
+	local sdkmanrc="$1"
+

Completion script initialisation problems
Using sdkman SDKMAN 5.11.2+698 on Ubuntu Linux 20.04 and bash 5.0.17(1) with the necessary code in .bashrc to put it in the path.

When I start a new terminal, i.e. invoke a new bash, output like the following *sometimes* appears on the console:

```
ommand not found
36m====: command not found

Command '0music' not found, did you mean:

  command 'music' from deb music-bin (1.1.16-1.1build2)

Try: sudo apt install <deb name>


Command '0music' not found, did you mean:

  command 'music' from deb music-bin (1.1.16-1.1build2)

Try: sudo apt install <deb name>


Command '0music' not found, did you mean:

  command 'music' from deb music-bin (1.1.16-1.1build2)

Try: sudo apt install <deb name>

================================================================================: command not found
```

I did not manage to find out why/when this happens, it appears to be almost random, though it usually happens when opening the *first* terminal after a restart or after a longer time. 

I have observed this behaviour for several weeks now and I am certain this only happens when the SDKMAN-related code is active in .bashrc, never happens when I comment that out. 

The "command not found"  complaints I get appear to come from strings inside the bash prompt definition and from the names of random directories in my home directory. I have no idea at all what could be going on here, but it became so annoying that I usually deactivate sdkman completely. 

So sadly, I cannot provide steps to reproduce because this problem occurs seemingly randomly (but often enough to be very annoying).

+includes_pathstar() {
+  while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
+    case $1 in (\*/* | \*\*/*)
+      return 0
+    esac
+    shift
+  done
+  return 1

+
+check_pathstar() {
+  while [ "$1" ]; do
+    case $1 in (\*/* | \*\*/*)
+      set -- "${1#*/}"
+      continue
+    esac
+    case $1 in (*\**)
+      return 1
+    esac
+    return 0
+  done
+  return 1

+  eval "$(shift 2; expand_pathstar_create_matcher "$@")"

+  expand_pathstar=$(shift; expand_pathstar_retrive '|||' "$@")
+  eval "$(expand_pathstar_iterator "$1" expand_pathstar '\|\|\|')"
+}
+
+expand_pathstar_create_matcher() {
+  echo "expand_pathstar_matcher() {"
+  for arg; do
+    pattern='' doublestar=''
+    while :; do
+      case $arg in
+        \*\*/*) arg=${arg#*/} doublestar=1 ;;
+        \*/*) arg=${arg#*/} pattern="${pattern}*/" ;;
+        *) break
+      esac
+    done
+
+    escape_quote arg "$arg"
+    if [ "$doublestar" ]; then
+      echo "  case \$1 in (${pattern}*)"
+      echo "    [ \"\${1##*/}\" = $arg ] && return 0"
+      echo "  esac"
+    elif [ "$pattern" ]; then
+      echo "  case \$1 in (${pattern}*)"
+      echo "    [ \"\${1#$pattern}\" = $arg ] && return 0"
+      echo "  esac"
+    else
+      echo "  [ \"\$1\" = $arg ] && return 0"
+    fi
+    echo ""
+  done
+  echo "  return 1"
+  echo "}"
+}
+
+expand_pathstar_retrive() {
+  finddirs "$2" ${SHELLSPEC_DEREFERENCE:+follow} | {
+    sep=$1 dir=${2%"${2##*[!/]}"}
+    [ "$dir" = "." ] && dir="" || dir="$dir/"
+    shift 2
+    for i; do
+      pattern=$i
+      case $i in
+        \*/* | \*\*/*)
+          while i=${i#*/}; do
+            case $i in (\*/* | \*\*/*) continue; esac
+            break
+          done
+          set -- "$@" "${i}${sep}${pattern}"
+          ;;
+        *) echo "${i}${sep}"
+      esac
+      shift
+    done

+  echo "  \"$1\" \"\${$2%$3*}\" \"\${$2##*$3}\""
+  echo 'done <''< HERE'
+  echo "\$$2"
+  echo 'HERE'

problem_statement:
A path syntax to match recursive directories (was Add -R, --recursive option)
This option find the path of the specfile recursively. For example, it is useful for directory structures such as the following.

Case 1
----

```
project-root/
├── app1/
│      └── spec/
├── app2/
│      └── spec/
└── app3/
       └── spec/
```

```console
$ cd project-root
$ shellspec
```

Case 2
----

```
project-root/
├── app1/
│      └── test_spec.sh
├── app2/
│      └── test_spec.sh
└── app3/
       └── test_spec.sh
```

```console
$ cd project-root

$ cat .shellspec
--default-path test_spec.sh

$ shellspec
```

+++ b/lib/core/subjects/fd.sh
@@ -0,0 +1,38 @@
+#shellcheck shell=sh
+
+shellspec_syntax 'shellspec_subject_fd'
+shellspec_syntax 'shellspec_subject_entire_fd'
+
+shellspec_subject_fd() {
+  shellspec_syntax_param count [ $# -ge 1 ] || return 0
+
+  # shellcheck disable=SC2034
+  SHELLSPEC_META='text'
+  SHELLSPEC_SUBJECT="$SHELLSPEC_STDIO_FILE_BASE.fd-${1}"
+  if [ -e "$SHELLSPEC_SUBJECT" ]; then
+    # shellcheck disable=SC2034
+    shellspec_capturefile SHELLSPEC_SUBJECT "$SHELLSPEC_SUBJECT"
+  else
+    unset SHELLSPEC_SUBJECT ||:
+  fi
+  shift
+
+  eval shellspec_syntax_dispatch modifier ${1+'"$@"'}
+}
+
+shellspec_subject_entire_fd() {
+  shellspec_syntax_param count [ $# -ge 1 ] || return 0
+
+  # shellcheck disable=SC2034
+  SHELLSPEC_META='text'
+  SHELLSPEC_SUBJECT="$SHELLSPEC_STDIO_FILE_BASE.fd-${1}"
+  if [ -e "$SHELLSPEC_SUBJECT" ]; then
+    # shellcheck disable=SC2034
+    shellspec_readfile SHELLSPEC_SUBJECT "$SHELLSPEC_SUBJECT"
+  else
+    unset SHELLSPEC_SUBJECT ||:
+  fi
+  shift
+
+  eval shellspec_syntax_dispatch modifier ${1+'"$@"'}
+}

problem_statement:
[RFE] Support custom file-descriptors in conditions
Hello,

Currently, we can only check for stdout / stderr content. In my library, I use a `log` function used for info/warning/error/trace/debug, and which is sent to a special file descriptor (in variable `$__AMMLOG_FDSTD`, by default fd 97)

Some functions skip bad content but provides a log message. I'd like to test this log message in my custom fd.

Would it be possible to implement something like  (not tested)

```
Describe "this is a test for custom filedescriptors"
  foo() { echo >&4 "Hello world"; }
  setup() { exec 4>&1; }
  Before 'setup'
  It "checks non-standard output"
    When call foo
    The status should be success
    The fd 4 should include "world"
  End
End
```

If the FD number can be a variable, that would be even better.

many thanks !

problem_statement:
Use default $HOME/.local install directory instead of $HOME/bin and $HOME/lib
In my Ubuntu .profile there is 
```
**# set PATH so it includes user's private bin if it exists
if [ -d "$HOME/bin" ] ; then
    PATH="$HOME/bin:$PATH"
fi

# set PATH so it includes user's private bin if it exists
if [ -d "$HOME/.local/bin" ] ; then
    PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
fi
**
```

And in the curl -fsSL https://git.io/shellspec installer, the default installation folders are $HOME/bin and $HOME/lib. And the lib folder is only used by shellspec contrary to my .local/lib which is used by a bunch of programs including python's module:
```
ls -l ~/.local/bin/
total 748
-rwxrwxr-x 1 jean jean    218 nov.   9 21:52 f2py
-rwxrwxr-x 1 jean jean    218 nov.   9 21:52 f2py2
-rwxrwxr-x 1 jean jean    218 nov.   9 21:52 f2py2.7
-rwxr-xr-x 1 jean jean    741 nov.  10 08:49 fluxgui
-rwxrwxr-x 1 jean jean   3770 nov.   9 22:01 mid3cp
-rwxrwxr-x 1 jean jean   5258 nov.   9 22:01 mid3iconv
-rwxrwxr-x 1 jean jean  14767 nov.   9 22:01 mid3v2
-rwxrwxr-x 1 jean jean   2479 nov.   9 22:01 moggsplit
-rwxrwxr-x 1 jean jean   1239 nov.   9 22:01 mutagen-inspect
-rwxrwxr-x 1 jean jean   3305 nov.   9 22:01 mutagen-pony
lrwxrwxrwx 1 jean jean     49 déc.   2 20:49 php -> /home/jean/.local/lib/docker-php-multiversion/php
-rwxrwxr-x 1 jean jean 706004 sept. 27  2013 xflux
```

This has one advantage: it keeps your home folder cleaner (Btw I copied this script for my php-multiversion tool and moved it to .local as default).

I just opened this bug as I don't know if your realized that but I think it would be a better place for installing shellspec. If you disagree, simply close it, my opinion is nothing more than my opinion

install.sh script fails on Travis CI Windows machines
The Windows machines on Travis CI are experimental and there is a bug with the `/dev/tty` device. But I think it will take a long time before it is fixed.

The `install.sh` script rely on the `/dev/tty` device. Is it possible to remove this dependency or find another way to make that script works on Travis CI Windows machines ?

See the Travis CI build below:
https://travis-ci.com/damienflament/travis-experiment/jobs/290440856#L43

+  eval shellspec_join SHELLSPEC_EXPECTATION '" "' Assert ${1+'"$@"'}

+  set +e

+  set "$1" -- $?

+      shellspec_on WARNED

problem_statement:
`Assert` expectation for custom assertion
ShellSpec already has `result of` modifier for custom assertion. It can be assert using custom function. However, it can not pass arguments and you might want a simpler custom assertion.

## Here are sample.

```sh
exists_docker_image() {
  docker inspect "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1
}

It "builds docker image"
  When run create_docker_image my_image
  Assert exists_docker_image my_image
End
```

## Planned specifications

Difference between `result of` and `Assert`.

The `result of` is

- custom assertion for result of evaluation.
  - That is, the arguments of the custom function are stdout, stderr, and status.

The `Assert` is

- custom assertion for external side effects.
  - That is, the arguments of the custom function are passed as is.
- You can not assert stdout/stderr/status of evaluation. 
  - To be exact, it is possible by using the variable `SHELLSPEC_STDOUT` etc, But not recommend because it is internal variable.
- Enable `errexit` before calling custom function.
  - To make it easy to assert without a `return` like bats.

NOTE: No plan to implement `AssertEqual` etc. Because it can be implemented with `Assert`.


Do you have any suggestion? or thumbs up if you like it.

http-serve does not work in Arch Linux
In Arch Linux, `/usr/bin/python` points to Python 3.x and not Python 2.x. So using `http-serve` results in the following error:

```
/usr/bin/python: No module named SimpleHTTPServer
```

I think there should be a way to select which Python interpreter to use, so Arch Linux users could set it to `/usr/bin/python2`. Another user case: some distros may not install Python by default, and the user may install Python in their home directory or `/opt`.

homebrew module regression

Originally the bail-out code was:
```zsh
if [[ "$OSTYPE" != (darwin|linux)* ]]; then
  return 1
fi
```

The regression is:
```zsh
if ! is-darwin || ! is-linux; then
  return 1
fi
```

Fix:
```zsh
if ! is-darwin && ! is-linux; then
  return 1
fi
```

problem_statement:
[fix PR submitted] kubectl hangs when running kubectl version with no context causing prompt to hang
### The problem

PR #1246 submitted for review with the fix outlined above in place and tested as working with both no context and a context, all works as normal once the fix is applied.

I think this is a recent problem, and through a few hours of debugging I cannot figure out why this behaviour has suddenly changed.

Now I understand this isn't a `spaceship-prompt` issue, but until whatever issue is resolved in kubectl, a workaround is required otherwise I have to wait around 10 seconds for the prompt to load everytime, which is an obvious frustration.

When using `kubectl` without a context it now hangs trying to connect to a null context resulting in the following error:

```sh
14:31:16 in ~
➜  echo $KUBECONFIG

14:31:20 in ~ took 10s
➜  kubectl version
WARNING: This version information is deprecated and will be replaced with the output from kubectl version --short.  Use --output=yaml|json to get the full version.
Client Version: version.Info{Major:"1", Minor:"25", GitVersion:"v1.25.0", GitCommit:"a866cbe2e5bbaa01cfd5e969aa3e033f3282a8a2", GitTreeState:"clean", BuildDate:"2022-08-23T17:44:59Z", GoVersion:"go1.19", Compiler:"gc", Platform:"darwin/arm64"}
Kustomize Version: v4.5.7
Unable to connect to the server: EOF

# 10 second hang
```

Using `brew`, I rolled back `kubectl` to prior versions (currently 1.25, but tried <1.22 as well) and this problem now seems to just keep occuring.

My proposed fix for this is to mirror the context check that occurs within `sections/kubectl_context.zsh` line 29-30 into `sections/kubectl_version.zsh` at line 27-28, prior to the version check. So the snippet reads:

```sh
# ...

  spaceship::exists kubectl || return

  # New context check that will exit out of the version check if no context is loaded, avoiding the hang
  # Code sourced from ~ sections/kubectl_context.zsh:29-30
  local kube_context=$(kubectl config current-context 2>/dev/null)
  [[ -z $kube_context ]] && return

  # if kubectl can't connect kubernetes cluster, kubernetes version section will be not shown
  local kubectl_version=$(kubectl version --short 2>/dev/null | grep "Server Version" | sed 's/Server Version: \(.*\)/\1/')
  [[ -z $kubectl_version ]] && return

# ...
```

PR #1246 submitted for review with the fix outlined above in place and tested as working.

### Relevant Zsh configuration

```zsh
This isn't the `~/.zshrc`, this is instead the output of `set -x` to debug ZSH's prompt loading:

+spaceship_kubectl:3> spaceship_kubectl_version
+spaceship_kubectl_version:1> [[ true == false ]]
+spaceship_kubectl_version:3> spaceship::exists kubectl
+spaceship::exists:1> command -v kubectl

+spaceship_kubectl_version:6> sed 's/Server Version: \(.*\)/\1/'

# hangs for upwards of 15 seconds before continuing
```

+#
+# Ansible
+#
+# Ansible is a suite of software tools that enables infrastructure as code.
+# Link: https://docs.ansible.com/ansible/latest/index.html
+
+# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Configuration
+# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+SPACESHIP_ANSIBLE_SHOW="${SPACESHIP_ANSIBLE_SHOW=true}"
+SPACESHIP_ANSIBLE_ASYNC="${SPACESHIP_ANSIBLE_ASYNC=true}"
+SPACESHIP_ANSIBLE_PREFIX="${SPACESHIP_ANSIBLE_PREFIX="$SPACESHIP_PROMPT_DEFAULT_PREFIX"}"
+SPACESHIP_ANSIBLE_SUFFIX="${SPACESHIP_ANSIBLE_SUFFIX="$SPACESHIP_PROMPT_DEFAULT_SUFFIX"}"
+SPACESHIP_ANSIBLE_SYMBOL="${SPACESHIP_ANSIBLE_SYMBOL="🅐 "}"
+SPACESHIP_ANSIBLE_COLOR="${SPACESHIP_ANSIBLE_COLOR="white"}"
+
+# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Section
+# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+spaceship_ansible() {
+  [[ $SPACESHIP_ANSIBLE_SHOW == false ]] && return
+
+  # Check if ansible is installed
+  spaceship::exists ansible || return
+
+  # Show ansible section only when there are ansible-specific files in current
+  # working directory.
+  # Here glob qualifiers are used to check if files with specific extension are
+  # present in directory. Read more about them here:
+  # https://zsh.sourceforge.net/Doc/Release/Expansion.html
+  local ansible_configs="$(spaceship::upsearch ansible.cfg .ansible.cfg)"
+  local yaml_files="$(echo ?(*.yml|*.yaml)([1]N^/))"
+  local detected_playbooks
+
+  if [[ -n "$yaml_files" ]]; then
+    detected_playbooks="$(spaceship::grep -oE "tasks|hosts|roles" $yaml_files)"
+  fi
+
+  [[ -n "$ansible_configs" || -n "$detected_playbooks" ]] || return
+
+  # Retrieve ansible version
+  local ansible_version=$(ansible --version | head -1 | spaceship::grep -oE '[[:digit:]]+\.[[:digit:]]+\.[[:digit:]]')
+
+  # Display ansible section
+  spaceship::section \
+    --color "$SPACESHIP_ANSIBLE_COLOR" \
+    --prefix "$SPACESHIP_ANSIBLE_PREFIX" \
+    --suffix "$SPACESHIP_ANSIBLE_SUFFIX" \
+    --symbol "$SPACESHIP_ANSIBLE_SYMBOL" \
+    "v$ansible_version"
+}

problem_statement:
Confusing "Permission denied" error when running `spaceship edit` with $EDITOR unset
### The problem

With `$EDITOR` unset, `spaceship edit` exits with a confusing error message.

```zsh
~
➜ spaceship edit
_spaceship::cli::edit:5: permission denied:

~
➜ echo $EDITOR


~
➜ echo $VISUAL


~
➜
```

Setting `$EDITOR` makes it work:

```zsh
~
➜ export EDITOR=cat

~
➜ spaceship edit
spaceship remove docker


~
➜
```

### Relevant Zsh configuration

```zsh
spaceship remove docker
SPACESHIP_EXIT_CODE_SHOW=true
SPACESHIP_VERSION=4.21.0
SPACESHIP_ROOT=/opt/homebrew/Cellar/spaceship/4.21.0
SPACESHIP_CONFIG=/Users/ebrannin/.config/spaceship.zsh

Please read our TROUBLESHOOTING page for commonly encountered problems:

https://github.com/denysdovhan/spaceship-prompt/blob/master/docs/Troubleshooting.md
-->

**Current behavior**

Battery section display improperly while the battery adapter plugged in but not charging (because battery level is equal or greater than 95%). And results in `•charging% ➜`

**Expected behavior**

It should display `➜`

#### Environment

**Spaceship version:** 3.11.1
**Zsh version:** 5.7.1 (x86_64-pc-linux-gnu)
**Zsh framework:** oh-my-zsh
**Zsh plugin manager:** None
**Terminal emulator:** gnome-terminal
**Operating system:** Linux manjaro 5.1.16-1-MANJARO

#### Screenshot

Provide a screenshot that shows your issue.

![screenshot](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/22719617/62630682-a308c680-b959-11e9-8314-fa027bfdab9d.png)

**Possible solution**
My `acpi` output:

- The adapter plugged in: `Battery 0: Not charging, 100%`
- The adapter is not plugged in: `Battery 0: Discharging, 100%, 07:14:35 remaining`

Index-based extraction results in the wrong token. `$4` should give `100%,` instead of `charging,`, what fails in adapter-plugged-in case.

We should use a pattern to precisely look up the battery level.
**Before**
```
battery_percent="$( echo $battery_data | awk '{print $4}' )"
```
**After**
```
battery_percent="$( echo $battery_data | awk '{ match($0, /[0-9]{1,3}%,?/, arr); print arr[0] }' )"
```

[maint]: Re-add `--no-pager` option to `zinit self-update`
### Summary

See https://github.com/zdharma-continuum/zinit/pull/173#discussion_r871271255.

``` sh
cd ~/.local/share/zinit/zinit.git
git reset --hard HEAD~300
```

Then, the following commands stop until user presses `q` to quit the pager.

``` sh
zinit self-update
# or
zinit self-update -q
```
